intuition: Try all course permutations and check their ordering. Topological removal determines feasibility in linear graph time. The feasibility question needs only one legal ordering, not a search over every permutation. Unmet prerequisite counts tell us which choices are currently legal.

Treat prerequisites as directed edges from the prerequisite to its dependent. A course with zero incoming edges can be taken immediately. Removing it fulfills one requirement for each dependent; a dependent becomes ready only when every incoming requirement has disappeared. A queue separates courses ready now from courses still blocked. If a disconnected component contains a cycle, other courses may finish normally but the completed count still exposes the unresolved component.

Every removed course has no prerequisites among the unremoved courses, so the removal order is legal. If all courses are removed, that order proves feasibility. Otherwise every remaining node has an incoming edge from another remaining node; repeatedly following predecessors in a finite graph reaches a cycle, which prevents completion. Adjacency lists hold edges; indegrees and the ready queue hold courses.
The queue is iterative. A valid chain of 2000 courses has traversal depth 2000, but this reference stores pending courses explicitly rather than consuming a Python recursive call for every edge.

steps: Build edges 0→1, 0→2, 1→3, and 2→3. Initialize indegrees [0,1,1,2], ready=[0], and completed=0.
Pop course 0 and set completed=1. Its outgoing edges reduce indegrees of 1 and 2 to zero, so ready becomes [1,2].
Pop course 1 and set completed=2. Course 3 still has indegree 1: finishing only one of its two prerequisites cannot release it.
Pop course 2 and set completed=3. Decrement course 3 to zero and enqueue it.
Pop course 3 and set completed=4. All courses finished, so completed==numCourses and the result is true.

codeNotes.note: Correct edge direction lets completing a prerequisite notify its dependents rather than its ancestors.
A course enters the queue only after all requirements are satisfied, not merely after the first prerequisite finishes.
Courses left blocked imply a cycle; counting also includes isolated courses that had no prerequisites.
